column1: # open-agent-robot — frozen fixture manifest (test item T-J3).
# Columns (tab-separated):  path <TAB> min_bytes <TAB> min_lines <TAB> sha256
#   path       relative to tests/fixtures/
#   min_bytes  size floor — a truncated fixture makes a replay test pass on no data
#   min_lines  line floor — the same defect one level up (a file of one long line)
#   sha256     the exact bytes that were annotated; an in-place edit of the same
#              length is invisible to both floors and only this catches it
# Verified by tests/test_fixture_manifest.py. Regenerate rows with
#   python tests/fixture_manifest.py --freeze
# which prints and never writes: a verifier that can rewrite its own expectations
# turns a corrupted fixture into a new baseline.
# Still outstanding: the 30 evaluation queries and the hand-annotated episode
# boundaries (S4, both blocked on a real log plus one human annotation pass).
# See tests/fixtures/README.md for what each present file is.
# On redteam.jsonl specifically: the hash freezes the bytes, and §6.0 rule 3 says the
# set only grows — so this row is EXPECTED to change when a line is added, and the
# review question on that diff is "was anything removed", which the min_lines floor
# also answers from below. A shrinking line count is the failure the floor catches
# without anyone having to read the hash.
README.md
redteam.jsonl
skill_triggers.tsv
why_goal_rejects.jsonl
